newsitem.title: USA: Nineteen die, thousands lose power in U.S. snowstorms.
newsitem.headline: Nineteen die, thousands lose power in U.S. snowstorms.

text.p: Snowstorms, ice and frigid temperatures from Texas across the U.S. Midwest have caused at least 19 deaths since Sunday and triggered power outages affecting thousands, authorities said Tuesday.
The nation will get a chilly break from the storms until Friday, when another storm system is expected to develop in western Texas and move northeast, meteorologists said.

The system is forecast to form early Friday and roll from Saturday through Monday across central Arkansas, southern Illinois and Indiana and into New England. Before that, cold weather should blanket much of the Midwest.

In the past two days, numerous deaths have been attributed in part to the weather, including those of two homeless men. Police said one man was found frozen to death in an alley behind a Dallas soup kitchen on Monday. Another man perished inside the cab of a pick-up truck in Oklahoma City.
A 52-year-old man was reportedly killed when his car rolled into a ditch in Butte County, South Dakota, on Monday. Bad weather played a role in the accident, police said.
Storms were involved in four traffic deaths across Missouri since Sunday night, said a highway patrol spokesman.
Earlier in the week, icy roads in western Michigan claimed two lives in traffic accidents.
Texas officials said at least nine people were killed in weather-related car accidents when a storm ripped through the state over the weekend, dumping up to six inches of snow.

In southwestern Minnesota, ice storms and powerful winds tore down power lines and snapped more than 1,500 utility poles. As many as 600 households in and around Worthington, Minnesota, were still without power Tuesday. Local officials said they planned to ask Minnesota Governor Arne Carlson to declare their portion of the state a disaster area.

Ice and heavy winds downed power lines across southern Oklahoma on Monday, cutting electricity to about 75,000 homes, but repair teams had restored power to all but 2,500 families by midday on Tuesday.
Hundreds of homes in southwest Missouri were without power Tuesday after storms downed power lines and trees. State police said at least one fatality resulted from the storm.
